There is no real integration or effective help from immigration. The Red Cross is the only one that still helps. They give work permits, but getting a job is practically impossible because your passport is retained and you can't verify your identity with the document they issue, the LMA. The LMA itself is not valid for identity verification within the Swedish immigration authority. When you ask about your passport, they say it can only be returned when the process is finalized. At the same time, to issue the coordination number, the temporary number, you need the passport. In other words, you are trapped in a contradictory system. They give, on average, 260 euros to buy food, personal hygiene items, breakfast, lunch, dinner, and everything else you might need. I don't recommend coming to Sweden now. Sweden is paying around 34,000 euros to those who have already obtained the document and are requesting to leave. Will they really do a fair exile assessment?

one_star_reviews.text: We had booked a VIP table for a hen party. But when the week came they didn't respond to messages and when we got there they hadn't put us on the list even though we had been confirmed 1 month before that they would do so.

Concert night at Cinco

+ free self-service Tap water with cups provided
+ central location
+ toilets ok
+ big venue with enough space to stand and/or sit down
+ impressive light and video LED elements
+ wardrobe incl. in ticket price

- customer communication:
We had tickets for a festival night. The event time was stated on the website and on our tickets from 17:00-21:00. As tourists in Umeå we had a very packed day already and arrived a little after 17:00, thinking we are too late to the event.

Inside the venue, other visitors were having dinner and there were no further signs of a concert happening, except an empty stage with drums and speakers.

One door had a light sign stating „live music ->“. We went there, but it lead us to another wine bar room. No signs of concert there as well.

I checked the ticket again and the website. All stating start 17:00. Only after searching and going to the event discussion section on Facebook and scrolling through it, I finally found a time table stating doors open 17:00, music begin 19:00.

Turned out, we were too early.

Nice, I thought - this gives me some time to relax after our long day. We sat down at a table. I felt my eyes closed down and started to have a small power nap. I let it happen because we still had an hour until the event starts.

Suddenly I was woken up from the waitress in a rough way, telling me: „This is a bar you can‘t sit here and sleep!“
I found it super unfriendly!
I don’t want to criticise the content of the message. But the way it was communicated. I understand that a bar is not a bed, but the way it was told felt rude. A friendly: „hi, I see that you are tired, could you please not sleep here? Can I maybe bring you a coffee?“ or „There is a more hidden place to sit in our venue. Could you Please go and relax there?“

—> Same message. Different words. Would have let to a different experience.

But no.

So, at that point I was tired and annoyed  before the event even started. My company and I eventually left to have a nap in the shopping mall near by and came back after a 20min power nap. We wanted to give it another chance.

So we went to the front of the stage, standing next to a fence which divided the room to a dance floor and the so called VIP lounge.
We danced, hugged and had fun until suddenly an older, clearly tipsy lady came to us from her couch in the VIP-lounge, telling us, that she took videos of the performance from her seat but that we disturbed her videos and are in her way and she asked us to go away so she can continue taking the videos while sitting there without disturbing her.
I thought I misunderstood.
Something like this never happened before to me.
So I asked: „What did you just say??“ she answered: „Oh nothing. No problem.“ and left back to her seat.

This situation, after the first encounter left us with an even worse feeling of not being welcome. Also here, I’m not criticising the content of the message but the way it was conveyed. Also, there was so much space to take a video from a different position.

I would have loved to leave the event at that point. However, it was my birthday present to my company and the tickets were very expensive. So we stayed a little longer and tried to make the best out of this disappointing evening.

- A subjective minus point: I found the sound super bad. There were resonances, distortions and some instruments couldn’t be heard at all. There was a sound technician who took care of the sound, unfortunately with not much success.

All in all, it could have been a nice evening but those happenings added up to leave us with a bad feeling of unfriendliness, not being welcome, disappointment and being annoyed. A bad experience we paid a lot of money for. Really sad.

—> we didn’t eat, so I can’t rate the food.

No stars.
Bought my car new in -23 at Bilbyter in Norrköping. After about two and a half years, i.e. in the autumn of -26, the car had problems with the radar. It started to turn off regardless of the weather and thus the adaptive cruise control became unusable. I applied for this as a warranty defect in November. At the workshop visit, it was stated that the car had been test driven and the front bumper had been removed and the radar inspected without finding any faults. The computer connection also showed that everything worked well. They still chose to believe my information. The radar would be calibrated. However, I was supposed to document and send pictures of the dashboard and the radar when the faults occurred, which I did. As soon as I left the workshop, I noticed that the bumper had not been removed, but I could easily do that, the radar would be calibrated.
Two weeks later I left the car for calibration. It would take two hours. When I returned, it turned out that nothing had been done. The reason was that the computer still showed that everything was working fine and then they would not be paid for the work from Hyundai Motor Company. I was told that if I returned with the same problem next time I would have to pay for the troubleshooting. This was now stated by another person. The person who decided on the calibration and to whom I sent pictures was nearby and pretended nothing had happened. I live just over fifty kilometers from Norrköping and do not go to the workshop unnecessarily. The treatment was condescending. They contacted Hyundai later and according to them the car is just “hypersensitive to weather” and nothing can be done about it. When later contacted by phone (to ask about the price for calibration) I asked how I could prove the radar problem but was more or less laughed at. I then chose to change workshop even though it is further away. They found the fault immediately. The car’s software was also updated and now this one also showed that there was a fault with the radar, it was pointing in the wrong direction. It eventually turned out that one of the brackets was damaged. The error has now been fixed, the radar calibrated and everything works perfectly as before.
I understand that technical errors can sometimes be difficult to identify. But this condescending attitude and the fact that people don't believe my information, even though I had a lot of experience with the car, is difficult for me to accept. People believe 100% in computer diagnostics. I hope that people read and recognize themselves and can improve customer service in the future. I will not service the car at Bilbyter in the future and my trust in Hyundai Motor Company has also been negatively affected.

Life-threatening inspections and total lack of competence – Warning!

If you are considering hiring DEKRA Quality Management AB for an "impartial opinion" or vehicle inspection – think again. My experience shows an astonishing incompetence that directly endangers road safety.

In my case, a workshop hired DEKRA to inspect a rim painting on my Tesla. This is what DEKRA performed:

1. Inspects wet cars
DEKRA's inspector approved the paint job, but at the same time wrote in black and white in his own report that the car was covered in "water beads" and that "the surfaces cannot be fully considered". Approving a paint job through rainwater drops violates the industry's own regulations (Paint Standard) which require a thoroughly cleaned surface.

2. Approves direct danger to life ("Risk of death")**
DEKRA approved a repaint where paint had been applied to the bolt holes of the rims. In its own inspection report, DEKRA itself had attached the official manual of the car manufacturer Tesla as an appendix. This manual explicitly states that incorrect processing is prohibited and carries **"WARNING: Risk of death"** because the wheel can come off. DEKRA did not even read its own appendix, but approved work that the car manufacturer warns is dangerous to life.

3. Has the wrong skills
A search at the Swedish Companies Registration Office reveals why the mistakes are made. DEKRA Quality Management AB is registered in its articles of association for "calibration and control of equipment". They therefore send out tool calibrators to assess advanced vehicle repairs.

When I pointed out these fatal mistakes to DEKRA's top management, their general counsel and CEO chose to officially stand behind the inspection and refused to withdraw the incorrect report.

A company that lives on quality inspection, but turns a blind eye to car manufacturers' death warnings and approves paintwork through water droplets, lacks all credibility. Dangerous and incompetent. Avoid!

Lawsuit Instead of Dream Home

In 2021, together with our architect, who collaborates with Rörvikshus, we had our dream home designed in the New England style. Due to bureaucratic delays, we unfortunately had to wait several years for the building permit, which we finally received in the summer of 2025.

We were supervised by the Swiss construction manager, Felix Hartmann. Even during the planning phase, we got the impression that individual requests were only reluctantly considered or not implemented at all. We increasingly felt that the communication was not very customer-oriented.

Nevertheless, we were very much looking forward to the planned start of construction on September 1, 2025. By August 2025, we had already finalized our construction financing, made down payments to the builder for the basement construction, and transferred the contractually agreed down payment of 20% of the house construction price to Rörvikshus. Furthermore, shortly before construction was scheduled to begin, we had two online meetings with the site manager and the managing director, Magnus Nilsson, in which we were assured of a successful start to construction and good cooperation.

It was all the more shocking, therefore, to receive an email just five days before the official start of construction informing us that Rörvikshus was terminating our collaboration. At the same time, we were informed that the 20% deposit we had already paid would be retained as "compensation" because, allegedly, payment deadlines had not been met. However, this had never been discussed or mentioned in any of our previous conversations.

This was a severe personal and financial blow for us. Instead of our long-awaited dream home, we now faced legal disputes, significant financial losses, and immense emotional distress.

Based on our experience, we strongly advise against working with Rörvikshus.

I am writing to  file a complaint regarding clearly racist treatment that took place at the Bauhaus branch, both inside the store and subsequently in its immediate surroundings, carried out by members of your staff.

On Thursday, April 24, I visited the store accompanied by my uncle. We are both Mexican. At the time of payment, the cashier asked to inspect our backpacks. We were the only individuals asked to do so and also the only ones who were visibly foreign. Although we found this unusual, we complied. The staff memer opened our backpacks and proceeded to handle and remove our personal belongings. Once it was confirmed that we were not taking any unpaid items, we were allowed to leave.

As we did not find everything we needed, we went to a nearby Biltema store, approximately five minutes away. We completed our purchases there and remained inside for a considerable amount of time, even having coffee in the store’s cafeteria. However, upon leaving—already in the parking lot—we were approached by three Bauhaus employees, who stated that they needed to inspect our backpacks again.

This occurred despite the fact that we had already been checked, had passed the exit detectors, and had at all times been cleared of any wrongdoing. We expressed that the situation felt discriminatory; nevertheless, we complied again since we had nothing to hide. In the parking lot, they placed our backpacks on the ground and once again removed our belongings, while questioning us about our origin, whether we held Swedish residency, and what our occupations were. After once more confirming that we had not committed any offense, they simply told us we could leave—without offering any apology.

I consider this treatment deeply unacceptable. Store personnel should not approach individuals outside the premises, search their belongings in a public space, or expose them in such a manner in front of others. These actions not only violate our dignity but also reinforce harmful stigmas toward foreigners, particularly those of Latin American appearance.

Furthermore, a search had already been conducted inside the store, we had passed all security systems, and other verification methods—such as security cameras—were available. If there had been any legitimate concern, the appropriate course of action would have been to contact the relevant authorities, rather than taking matters into their own hands in a public setting.

We chose to cooperate at all times because we are aware that, in situations like this, resistance can often escalate matters. However, this does not justify the treatment we received.

My relative lives in this country, and it is deeply troubling that they must face this kind of treatment on a regular basis. As for myself, I am visiting, and this experience has left me with a profoundly negative impression. Rather than feeling welcomed, I felt targeted and scrutinized solely because of my appearance.

What occurred is neither minor nor isolated. Practices like these contribute to normalizing discrimination in ways that directly impact the everyday lives of racialized individuals. They send a clear and troubling message—that certain bodies are automatically considered suspicious, that some people must be monitored and controlled regardless of any actual wrongdoing. These experiences do not merely cause momentary discomfort; they erode trust, undermine any sense of belonging, and limit one’s ability to move through public spaces with a basic sense of safety and dignity.

This was a humiliating experience with tangible consequences. Despite needing to continue our purchases, we have chosen not to return to the store in order to avoid being subjected to similar treatment.

It is deeply concerning that racism can come to shape even the most basic aspects of daily life, such as the ability to shop freely, and that it does so through practices that should be unacceptable in any environment that claims to uphold respect and inclusion.

I went to Svalövs Pistolklubb because I had a long-standing interest in pistol shooting and was really looking forward to becoming a member. I was genuinely excited and happy to finally start shooting on a range in Sweden, especially since I had previously tried the sport abroad and had always had a strong interest in it. Unfortunately, the experience turned out to be one of the most unpleasant and discriminatory situations I have ever been in.

As soon as I arrived, I was met by the instructor Jonathan, who immediately made me feel unwelcome. I greeted him kindly but received a cold response. A few minutes later, a Swedish guy came in and his whole demeanor changed in an instant - he was suddenly happy, nice, social and welcoming.

When we sat in the room and he talked about the course, the difference was even more noticeable. As soon as he talked about the club, the community or general information, he directed himself at the other guy. But every time something negative was mentioned about police records, gun regulations, or the fact that guns are not used for self-defense, he turned to me, stared at me, and spoke as if the comments were directed at me personally, even though I had never said anything inappropriate at all.

It was as if I had been put in a box from the very first second and judged based on prejudice instead of being treated like a normal person who wanted to start the sport. The atmosphere became extremely uncomfortable and you really felt that you were not wanted there.

Later, another instructor came out with us. Then the person asked the Swedish guy: “Are you the only one who is going to test?” The Swedish guy’s father immediately noticed how strange the situation was and had to correct him by saying: “No, both of you.”

The fact that even other people in the room reacted says a lot about how clear the treatment was.

I went there with joy and anticipation but left feeling belittled, made suspicious and discriminated against. Instead of being met with respect and professionalism I was met with what felt like pure racism and lots of prejudice.

I would absolutely not recommend anyone to go to this club if they want to feel welcome or treated fairly.

My husband and I bought a cabinet for 2800 kr. and used Handyhand to find help with the assembly. We get in touch with a “handyhand” who says he has the job completely under control.

During the assembly, he suddenly tells us that he has assembled the back of the cabinet incorrectly, but at the same time says that it “doesn’t matter”. When he has to lift the cabinet further in the process, the entire cabinet ends up breaking.

The handyman then claims that it must be a manufacturing defect. However, when we contact the store where the cabinet was purchased, we are told that the damage is due to incorrect assembly, and therefore they do not cover it.

We then contact the handyman again, but he refuses to take responsibility. We then try to get help through Handyhand’s customer service,
which is almost impossible. They are extremely difficult to get in touch with and seem completely indifferent to our situation.

After a lot of back and forth, they ask us to fill out a damage compensation statement. The only problem is that the link on their website doesn't work. So we have to write to them once again and wait for a response before they finally send a working link.

In the damage compensation statement, we attached ALL the evidence:

- Pictures of the broken cabinet, etc.

- The answer from the handyman

- As well as a response from the store, which clearly confirms that the damage is due to incorrect assembly and not a manufacturing defect.

Yet we get the message that they will NOT cover the damage. Their explanation is that they only cover "damage during the task", but that this is simply "an incorrect assembly that we are dissatisfied with".

Excuse me... INCORRECT ASSEMBLY THAT WE ARE DISSATISFIED WITH?! How is a broken cabinet worth 2800 kr. not damage?

The most frustrating thing is that we didn't even have the opportunity to respond or comment on their decision. The case was simply closed without us really having the opportunity to explain ourselves further or defend ourselves against their assessment.

In addition to the terrible customer service and total lack of responsibility, we also had to pay 100 DKK to cancel the job.

We have to pursue this case further because the treatment we have received is completely unacceptable. No one should be left with a broken piece of furniture, an extra bill and a customer service that refuses to take responsibility, even when there is clear evidence.

This is honestly a complete scam. It seems like a platform that is only interested in money, while the customers are left with the bill and the problems themselves.

A truly shockingly bad experience. You should be ashamed of yourself.

Warning: Cheap rims but - they become EXTREMELY expensive in the long run!

I bought complete winter wheels (tires + rims) for my Tesla Model 3 from ABS Wheels a few years ago.

When it was time to change the wheels after the winter, it turned out that almost all of the ABS Wheels "special nuts" included had rusted really hard. The quality of these is completely unacceptable: the rust (we have road salt in Sweden) had eaten so deep that most of the nuts simply came off when they were to be loosened (see picture), despite almost excessive caution after the first nut came off.

I visited the ABS Wheels store in Rosersberg who happily announced that the only thing they could do is sell me new nuts(!)

Sure, the rims are OK looking, but my expensive experience shows that it has become much cheaper to buy originals, with real nuts, because even the tires last significantly longer than ABS Wheels rims.

After considerable difficulty finding a mechanic willing to take on the tedious job of drilling out broken nuts (and a hefty bill for several hours of work!) the rims are of course discarded, so I also have to buy new rims for next winter.

Saving a few hundred kronor and then having to spend tens of thousands of kronor to get rid of rusted junk is a bad deal.

I want to warn other buyers – Look elsewhere for quality that lasts and won't ruin your car.

ABS Wheels do not follow the recommendations of the Swedish National Board of Consumer Complaints (ARN). They are frequently found on Råd & Rön's black list. Should be avoided if you are not looking for problems.

Many master’s programs are heavily concentrated with students from a few countries, like India and Pakistan, so the “international environment” often feels more like marketing than reality.

The teaching quality was disappointing, and most lecturers seemed out of touch with industry standards or practical knowledge.

For students hoping to build a career after graduation, the value is questionable. Job opportunities in Sweden are limited, and the university’s teaching and reputation do not seem strong enough to offset that challenge.

If you are paying large tuition fees, think carefully before choosing this place. There are better universities, better study destinations and better ways to invest your money and time. Think of doing some internships, taking a break from job, and study yourself, rather than enrolling in a university. Sweden is a nice country, with nice people, but this university did not live up to the image it promotes.
But if you are already from Sweden, and your fee is payed by government, then why not, give it a try.! Not worth it, if you are going to pay half a million kronor for studying.

I would like to raise serious concerns about my experience at Halmstad University, specifically in the Master’s programme in Industrial Management and Innovation.

The academic and administrative environment in this programme has been extremely disappointing. In a class of only 21 students, groups were assigned with 5 members each. However, there was no proper monitoring or guidance from the teachers. As a result, students formed their own groups, and one student was completely excluded and isolated.

What is more concerning is that this student faced teasing and a lack of support from peers, even from students of the same country. When the issue was reported to the student council, no action was taken, and the response was that they could not help in this matter. Even more troubling, the teacher also did not intervene and instead contributed to the negative environment.

Additionally, there have been serious issues with academic fairness and communication. One teacher was frequently absent and failed the student. Later, the same teacher asked the student to redo the work on a different topic, promising better marks. Despite completing the work again, the student has still not received the results. Even after sending numerous emails over three semesters, there has been no response or resolution.

This situation raises serious questions about accountability, student support, and academic standards. For international students, especially those who depend on education loans and financial support from their families, delays like being told to “complete it next year” are not practical or acceptable.

This experience has caused significant stress, financial burden, and uncertainty about the future. It is deeply concerning that such issues are not addressed in a reputed institution.

I hope this feedback highlights the need for better management, fair evaluation, and stronger student support systems…

Your management has already ruined one student’s life. Nothing can change it now, but thank you for your response.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointed with the quality and long term durability of the DalaFloda HardPine 25x159 Premium Pearl flooring from Sveden Trä AB. This floor is marketed as a premium product, but after around one year of normal residential use it already started looking worn, patchy, and visually degraded. The white pigmented finish simply does not hold up over time. Even small scratches, normal wear, or localized cleaning quickly expose a dull grey tone underneath the surface, making the floor look uneven and aged far earlier than expected.

What is especially frustrating is that the floor cannot realistically be restored once this starts happening. I genuinely tried to maintain it correctly and followed the supplier’s guidance carefully. I used the exact products recommended to me, including Osmo Vask og Pleiemiddel, Osmo Vedlikeholdsvoks 3087 Hvit, Osmo Underhållsolja 3440 Hvit, Osmo Rens, Osmo Dekorvoks Snø, and Osmo hardvoksolje with white pigmentering. None of these products were capable of rebuilding the original Pearl finish in a convincing or controlled way. The white maintenance products contain too little pigment to properly repair worn areas, while Dekorvoks Snø creates visible tonal inconsistencies and patchiness. Instead of restoring the floor naturally, every attempt at maintenance leaves the surface looking more cloudy, uneven, and artificially repaired.

The technical guidance and follow up support were also disappointing. I clearly explained which products and methods I had already tested without success, yet the same ineffective recommendations were repeated again afterward. I was also initially guided toward standard white pigmented maintenance products, while it later became clear that the correct tone for this floor should have been much closer to Snø. On a heavily pigmented decorative floor system, that is a major detail to get wrong and suggests a lack of precision and understanding regarding their own maintenance system.

This floor simply does not age well. After roughly one year it already looked significantly degraded, and there appears to be no reliable way to restore the intended appearance once the pigment layer begins to break down. For a floor sold as a premium hardwax oiled solution, both the material quality and the technical support fall far below expectations. DalaFloda HardPine Premium Pearl is, in my experience, an overly sensitive and poorly engineered finish system that becomes grey, patchy, and unattractive far too quickly. I would absolutely not recommend this floor to anyone expecting durability, maintainability, or long term visual consistency.

In recent years, prices have been raised time and again. But at the same time, service and selection have gotten worse and worse.

I understand that inflation requires higher prices. But quality should not go down because of that.

The service is beyond criticism. The employees hardly greet you and they don't seem to care much.

The biggest problem, however, is the buffet. They have started to implement a system where they never put in/refill with new pizza until there are many customers. They are incredibly stingy with new pizzas and they usually run out immediately.

In the past, it never really ran out. And the few times it did run out, well, there was a new pizza ready right away.

Nowadays, the nonchalant staff just stands there and watches. They don't seem the least bit concerned that their food is out and that half the restaurant is waiting for new pizza. They don't say anything to us who are waiting, they just stand there and look completely unperturbed.

And at a buffet, I actually don't think the food should "run out" like it does here. It definitely gets refilled and I understand that you can't always have 10 pizzas in line. But I shouldn't have to wait 10 minutes for refills at a pizza buffet.

A real shame actually. Was a place we went to once a week before and I still think the pizzas are really good. If I had written a review 3 years ago it would have been 5/5.

But unfortunately it's no longer worth it considering the service and the poorly filled buffet.

Do not recommend.

I wish I had listened more to my ominous gut feeling when the person who took the measurements for the countertop came in, reeking of perfume, and pulled out the measuring stick. An error of about 0.5 meters. Which I discovered and informed about when I reviewed the drawings. Not a hint of an apology for the errors or the delay this meant. Not a thank you for saving them from having to manufacture a countertop incorrectly.

I was also more or less called a fool by the measuring man because I had already bought a sink. Apparently it was to be purchased from the stone company according to him and there were only 2 models that had printed low-resolution images on them. It was later resolved and they sent our ho but the worry of throwing 6000 down the drain was no fun to have.

It has been painfully obvious that neither the measuring man nor Falu Stenhuggeri had a handle on their process or product. There was also no information available to the customer. Most of the questions could have been cleared up directly at the time of measurement if they had known what the countertop manufacturer needed for information, but instead there were supplementary questions that caused the time to be extended further.

During the installation, one of the stone parts was wrong and a new part had to be cut and sent directly to us which took 3 weeks.
A compliment to the guys who brought in all the stone. The heaviest must have weighed over 150 kg which they took 2 men. Could it even be legal in terms of the work environment? Doubtful. They get 5 out of 5 stars. Nice, strong and accommodating.

When asked about compensation for delayed delivery, I was told that the time from approval of the drawing to installation is normally 4-6 weeks and now it was 7 weeks (10 weeks for the incorrectly cut part). Which they considered ok. That is, the statement that it would take 3-4 weeks from measurement to installation was incorrect and misleading from the beginning, as it took about 1 week from measurement to the opportunity for me to approve the drawings.

I normally do not write reviews and if Falu Stenhuggeri had taken responsibility and ownership for the delays, had better customer service and had apologetic compassion for us as a customer who had been without a kitchen for significantly longer than desired, I would never have written this.

The stone was nice, but I would not have chosen Falu Stenhuggeri when buying a countertop if I had to do it again. A real shame as I want to support local, smaller companies.

I followed the maintenance guidance provided and used Osmo Rens, Osmo Vask og Pleiemiddel, Osmo Vedlikeholdsvoks 3087 hvit, Osmo Underhållsolja 3440 hvit, and Osmo Dekorvoks and hardvoksolje. The system fundamentally lacks the ability to be maintained or restored in a controlled and predictable way.

This indicates a lack of precision in product knowledge and guidance.
This floor does not age well. The deterioration is clearly visible over time, and there is no reliable method to bring it back to its intended appearance. For a premium product, both the material performance and the technical support fall short.
DalaFloda is owned by Svedentra, which is why I am posting this here. They deserve to hear this.

I bought the last copies of ACOUSTICAL PANEL STANDARD WALNUT 2400x520x18 mm. Before the purchase, the seller checked the stock balance in the system and assured me that a new delivery would arrive within 1-2 weeks.

After some time, I contacted the customer service center and was told that the product would not be available again.

Instead of a solution, I was suggested to go to another Bauhaus, about 200 km away, to try to buy the missing panels there.

In practice, this means that I have to tear down what I have already installed and buy completely new panels to be able to complete the project.

Unfortunately, I will not be shopping at Bauhaus again.

Ugh, no one should have to feel that way, especially not while trying on their wedding dress! Steer clear.

This was really not a good experience. Had to pay for troubleshooting my son's computer where they found no fault and therefore could not fix it. They also added that if we were not satisfied we could go somewhere else. When I later that month had the computer fixed in Stockholm where they both identified the fault (after 1 minute!) and fixed it the same day, I understood how abysmal Macforum in Jönköping is. That they are allowed to represent Apple is unimaginable. Avoid this business.

I am very dissatisfied with my experience at Niemi Bil in Umeå.

I paid extra for their workshop to install an engine heater cable and assumed that the work was done correctly. When I later returned the car for annual service at Toyota, I was told that the installation was incorrect – even a potential fire hazard. This feels completely unacceptable.

When I bought it, they also claimed that the car had been fully serviced. When I checked this with Toyota afterwards, it turned out that this was not true.

In addition, there was a dent on the bodywork that I was promised feedback on for action. That feedback never came, even though I waited and followed up.

I really cannot recommend Niemi Bil, especially not to people with less knowledge of cars. There is a great risk that you will be misled and have to pay extra for problems that the company itself caused. Very unserious attitude and handling.
